result:
No. Don't add Redis here.

One Elixir process with a single writer already gives you serialized access without a lock service, and SQLite-on-boot already covers durability. Redis would solve neither problem, and it would add a second source of truth plus a network failure domain that your current design doesn't have.

For in-memory caching, ETS gives you the same read speed in-process, with no serialization cost and no separate deployment.

Revisit if one of these becomes true: you run more than one node and need shared state or a distributed lock, you need pub/sub across hosts, or working-set size outgrows the BEAM heap and you need eviction you'd rather not build.
